spec.title: VSCode extension YOLO mode - read Claude settings and pass --dangerously-skip-permissions flag
spec.context: Users who have YOLO mode enabled in Claude's settings (via .claude/settings.json or ~/.claude/settings.json) still get prompted for permissions when using the kanban extension. The extension creates terminals and runs `claude "/kanban-..."` commands, but doesn't pass the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag even when the user has configured Claude for bypass permissions mode. This creates friction for users who've opted into YOLO mode and expect seamless workflow matching their Claude configuration.

in-scope.item: Detect YOLO mode via "dangerously-skip-permissions": true OR "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions"
Pass --dangerously-skip-permissions flag when creating terminal commands
Project-level settings take precedence over global settings
Create new settings capability following existing architecture

out-of-scope.item: UI for configuring YOLO mode (uses existing Claude settings)
Caching or file watching (read on every command for real-time updates)
Error notifications to user (silent degradation to normal behavior)

requirements.requirement: The system shall read .claude/settings.json from the workspace root when executing kanban commands
The system shall read ~/.claude/settings.json from the user's home directory as fallback when project-level settings don't exist
The system shall detect YOLO mode when settings contain "dangerously-skip-permissions": true (strict equality)
The system shall detect YOLO mode when settings contain "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions" (exact string match)
The system shall prepend --dangerously-skip-permissions flag to claude commands when YOLO mode is detected
The system shall use project-level settings when both project and global settings exist
The system shall default to normal behavior (no flag) when settings files don't exist or are unparseable
The system shall read settings before each command execution for real-time updates

files.file: New capability for reading Claude settings files. Uses FileSystemCapability for file I/O. Returns parsed settings or null on error.
Pure logic computer for determining YOLO mode from settings object. Handles precedence logic and strict equality checks.
Initialize settings capability in activate(). Update 5 command locations (lines 262, 279, 289, 307, 322) to read settings and conditionally add flag.

patterns.pattern: Use factory function with FileSystemCapability injected for testability. Reference: apps/vscode/src/capabilities/file-system.capability.ts:16-48
File I/O in capability, pure logic in computer. Capabilities handle HOW, computers handle WHAT. Reference: .kanban/engineering/patterns/capability-computer.md:33-49
Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch with type guard: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) Reference: apps/kanban/src/scripts/get-skill-config.ts:40-62
Use os.homedir() + path.join() for platform-agnostic home directory resolution. Reference: apps/vscode/src/capabilities/file-system.capability.ts:37-39
All factory functions define explicit return type interfaces. Reference: .kanban/engineering/patterns/factory-di.md:65-72

product.finding: Terminal capability sends commands via sendText(). Commands formatted as `claude "/kanban-..."`. Flag must be inserted before command path.
Extension works across multiple entry points (CodeLens, command palette, header buttons, tree view). All route through terminal capability.

engineering.finding: Three-layer architecture: Orchestrator (extension.ts), Capabilities (I/O), Computers (pure logic). Settings reading should be a capability.
Capabilities handle mechanism (file reading), orchestrators make policy decisions (when to add flag).

codebase.finding: Terminal capability at apps/vscode/src/capabilities/terminal.capability.ts provides sendCommand() that calls terminal.sendText()
File system capability at apps/vscode/src/capabilities/file-system.capability.ts provides readFile(), exists(), joinPath()

pitfall.mitigation: Use os.homedir() + path.join() for platform-agnostic resolution
Read settings on every command execution for real-time updates
Check project .claude/settings.json first, fallback to global ~/.claude/settings.json
Strict equality (=== true for dangerously-skip-permissions, === 'bypassPermissions' for defaultMode)
Create new claude-settings.capability.ts following existing architecture
Check with fs.existsSync() before reading, default to normal behavior
Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch, default to normal behavior on error
Wrap file read in try-catch, silently degrade to normal behavior
Silent degradation matches existing extension pattern (no error UI)

constraints.constraint: Use only Node.js built-ins (fs, path, os) - no new npm dependencies
Silent degradation on errors - no error UI (matches extension philosophy)
No caching - read settings fresh on each command for real-time updates
Must work across all 5 command execution paths in extension.ts

external.dependency: Node.js os module (needs import for homedir())

risk.mitigation: Check existence before reading, silent fallback to normal behavior

risks.risk: Settings file doesn't exist for new users

risk.mitigation: Slight I/O cost acceptable for real-time accuracy

risks.risk: Performance impact from reading on every command
